articles.title: ‘RuneScape’-Inspired Animation Series in the Works From Lyrical Animation and Jagex
articles.summary: Lyrical Animation is developing a new animation series based on “RuneScape” in partnership with creator Charlie “MoistCr1TiKaL” White and game developer Jagex, the company’s CEO Jon Bellamy announced on stage at RuneFest in Birmingham, UK, on Saturday.
body: Jagex first released “RuneScape” in 2001, and it has grown into a massively popular fantasy multiplayer online role-playing game. Through quests, combat, exploration and cooperative adventures, players can forge their own paths through the medieval fantasy world of Gielinor. The franchise now includes “RuneScape,” “Old School RuneScape” and “ RuneScape Dragonwilds.”

White is a longtime member of the “RuneScape” community and has amassed more than 25 million followers across his channels and platforms. “I’ve been playing RuneScape for 22 years, and it’s one of my favorite IPs ever,” said White. “I’m so excited to be working with the team on this project.”

“RuneScape has such a unique storytelling voice, at once laugh-out-loud funny and effortlessly insightful,” said Daniel Dominguez, creative director of Lyrical Animation. “To be allowed to help bring that to life for its millions of fans alongside our dear friend Charlie again is a dream come true.”
Lyrical Animation will produce the project alongside White’s Meatier Productions. Development is in its early stages, and the company expects to reveal more details in 2027.

articles.title: Guillermo Del Toro Defends ‘Digger,’ Calls the Film ‘Daring, Bold and Cinematically Complex’
articles.summary: Guillermo Del Toro is publicly declaring his love for “Digger.” Del Toro took to X to call out naysayers of Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s film ahead of its Friday release. “Entirely Petty headline,” the director wrote in response to a review of Warner Bros.’ R-rated black comedy. “Love it or not.
body: “Funny, I go into the platform and without even scrolling down, these are popping at the top of my timeline…” he wrote alongside the repost. “So… I will just keep posting them. Tune in or drop out—” In another repost, he wrote, “Dig or Die – c’mon!”

Del Toro also compared the negative reviews of “Digger” to those of “The Big Lebowski,” “The King of Comedy,” and “The Counselor,” all of which drew scrutiny at release but later found appreciation with audiences.

“Digger” is currently at just 51% on Rotten Tomatoes. Variety ’s chief film critic Owen Gleiberman said that, although the film feels like a comedy, it failed to actually be funny. “I’m not sure that ‘Digger’ is going to connect, because it’s so full of itself — so top-heavy with importance,” Gleiberman wrote in his review. “The movie cost north of $125 million to make, and that figure is not only too big to probably justify itself; it’s a testament to the arrogance of the filmmakers — to the assumption that we’ll turn out in droves for this ponderous absurdist lecture.”

articles.summary: Tony Gilroy blasted the “tragic” nature of the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger at the world premiere of his new film, “Behemoth!” Produced on a $36 million budget, “Behemoth!” is representative of the mid-budget, adult-oriented drama that once sustained Hollywood’s theatrical business — and allowed…
body: Skydance has tentatively set Tuesday, Oct. 6, to close the merger, which will consolidate Hollywood’s traditional Big Five studios (Disney, Universal, Sony, Warner Bros. and Paramount) under just four corporate owners. While Ellison has maintained that Paramount and Warner Bros. will retain their separate studio identities under Skydance, industry figures — including “Behemoth!” producer Sanne Wohlenberg — fear the consolidation will make the “possibilities for a filmmaker alarmingly limited.”

“God, it’s certainly turbulent and uncertain times, isn’t it? It never seems to get any easier,” Wohlenberg said. “I do think you have to take a deep breath and keep believing that things will be circular and come back. When you look at history, there have been many, many bad times. Sadly, we are steering into one, which will make the competitive nature of the industry and possibilities for a filmmaker alarmingly limited. And it shouldn’t be like that. I think we will survive it and I hope for better times.”

articles.title: Pierre Le Gall’s Passionate Love Story ‘Flesh and Fuel’ Named Best Film at Zurich Film Festival
articles.summary: French director Pierre Le Gall’s passionate love story “Flesh and Fuel,” which world premiered in Cannes’ Critics’ Week, won the top prize, the Golden Eye, at the 22nd Zurich Film Festival on Saturday.
body: The film stars Alexis Manenti, who won a César for Most Promising Actor for “Les Misérables.”

The jury stated, “At a time when isolation has become a means of protecting ourselves from the world and from one another, ‘Flesh and Fuel’ offers a compelling and deeply cinematic reflection on the fundamental human need for connection. With exquisite sensitivity, the film explores how the desire to love and be loved demands that we confront and ultimately break through the physical and emotional boundaries we construct around ourselves.”
The narrative film jury was comprised of directors Cary Joji Fukunaga and Fernando Eimbcke, actress Ella Rumpf, producer Julie Billy and Walter Fasano, director, film editor and screenwriter.
Special mentions went to Mads Mengel’s “The Guest” and Zou Jing’s “A Girl Unknown.”

articles.title: Florence Pugh on How Zoe Kazan ‘East of Eden’ Collaboration Helped Boost Her Confidence
articles.summary: The actress who plays the central character of Cathy and serves as an executive producer on the well-reviewed Netflix adaptation was Kazan's first and only choice for the role: "I didn't have a backup."
body: When Zoe Kazan set out to adapt East of Eden into what would become the seven-episode Netflix limited series, she only had one actress in mind for the central role of Cathy Ames: Florence Pugh.
“I didn’t have a backup,” Kazan previously told Netflix. “I didn’t have another person that I thought would be just as good. She is the exact right person to play Cathy.”

“The way that Cathy Ames is described in the book is kind of doll-like but with something icy or steely underneath,” Kazan told The Hollywood Reporter at East of Eden ‘s New York premiere Wednesday night. “And I felt in Florence this mix of a very feminine presentation with, in a Jungian sense not in a gender sense, of masculinity to her soul. That she had a lot of raw emotion and agency and action, which is very Cathy to me.”

“I feel like that performance announced a generational talent,” she said. “I think she’s a genius. It was very clear to me that, even though that character is very different from Cathy, if she can do that magic trick of a performance, she can do this.”

articles.title: Annabelle Wallis on the Defining Question of ‘Unabomber,’ a Potential James Wan Reunion and ‘Peaky Blinders’ What-Ifs
articles.summary: Plus: how an old The Hollywood Reporter interview with Wallis sparked a false viral story about the real-life Annabelle doll escaping the Warren Museum in Connecticut.
body: Annabelle Wallis has long considered herself an outsider, but she still has a knack for getting inside Hollywood’s most impenetrable personas.

She may look like she’s from Southern California and sound quintessentially English, but the Oxford-born actor’s heart and sensibility belong to Portugal, where she spent her formative years before returning to the U.K. at 17 to pursue an acting career. That cultural duality made her early casting endeavors more challenging than anticipated.

The end of 2013 proved to be a game-changer when she debuted as an undercover Irish cop named Grace Burgess opposite Cillian Murphy’s Tommy Shelby in Steven Knight’s BBC series Peaky Blinders. Posing as a barmaid at the Birmingham gangster’s favorite watering hole, she soon found herself caught between her assignment and her growing feelings for Tommy, eventually becoming the love of his life. The first season was critically well received, but it wasn’t a ratings juggernaut (yet).

articles.title: Noel Gallagher guitar sells for £12,000 at auction
articles.summary: The instrument was one of a number of items which belonged to a former Oasis sound engineer.
body: A guitar which originally belonged to Noel Gallagher has been sold for £12,000 at auction.
The limited edition Epiphone instrument in Manchester City blue was one of a number of items put up for sale by the son of Huw Richards, a former front-of-house sound engineer with the band.
Another of the items in his collection, a Kangol rain jacket produced for the band's touring personnel, sold for £2,000.
But a set of unheard Oasis recordings valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m were pulled from the auction last week, after the band filed an injunction.

articles.title: Alison Hammond returns home from hospital after rushing off This Morning
articles.summary: The This Morning presenter said she believes she experienced a panic attack on Friday's show.
body: Alison Hammond has said she is home and "feeling so much better" after she went to hospital for a heart check-up after leaving ITV's This Morning midway through Friday's show.

The presenter, 51, left the programme during its live broadcast, appearing to clutch her chest as she was helped off set by co-host Dermot O'Leary. He later told viewers she was "feeling a little unwell".
Soon after Hammond said she had "a little bit of a palpitation" and was undergoing tests.
In a video on Instagram on Saturday, she said she was "all OK, all-clear, which would mean I had a massive panic attack on live TV. I mean, the shame of it."

articles.title: Stephen King Says This Underrated Vampire TV Show Is Based On An Even Better Book
articles.summary: Stephen King is a fan of this underrated horror series and the book that inspired it. Then again, the book was written by his son.
body: At this point, Stephen King is as prolific a recommender of TV shows and movies as he is an author. King only just delivered a glowing review of the underseen Apple TV series "Last Seen" which followed his endorsement of Netflix horror miniseries "My Sad Dead." Now, he's back with yet another dispatch from his travels in the streaming sphere. According to the writer, the supernatural horror drama "NOS4A2" is well worth a watch, but he would say that since it's based on a book written by his son.
King's latest rec comes via his Threads account, where he anticipated responses from those who might claim he had a biased opinion.

As King sees it, "NOS4A2" is a "cool TV series" but it's the book to which we should all be paying close attention. The "incredibly tense & scary" novel of the same name was first published by his son, Joe Hill, back in 2013. The writer's third novel follows a woman with a supernatural gift who becomes the target of a similarly supernatural killer who feeds on the souls of children. In King's view, the novel is well worth a read regardless of his relationship to its author. But the TV show received solid reviews and is arguably underrated, too.

articles.title: Ted Lasso's Downfall Can Be Traced Back To One Moment
articles.summary: Ted Lasso hasn't been the same since its zeitgeist-grabbing first season. Here's the episode where the show passed the point of no return.
body: I suspect most viewers know that the series hasn't ever recaptured the highs of Season 1, but when did its downfall really begin? I've pinpointed the specific episode where it passed the point of no return: Season 2, Episode 7, "Headspace." That's when it became clear the show had taken two distinct wrong turns, and my stomach dropped when I realized we were going to have to watch the consequences of both of them play out over the course of multiple episodes.

When Ted starts suffering from panic attacks in Season 2, and therapy enters the picture, the tenor of the series changes dramatically — and not for the better. I won't speak for everyone, but for me, the show wildly misjudged how interested I was in exploring its lead character's interior struggles — especially when, and this feels harsh to say, but, to use therapy-speak, I have to "speak my truth," Ted's struggles aren't even that compelling. Everyone has a different tolerance for this stuff, but for me, this decision changed the DNA of the show for a while, and it never fully recovered.

articles.summary: There was a murder and a recruitment in the latest episode, and that was just in the opening minutes.
body: Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.
A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.
As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.
